[**✓**]{.mk-d} the story is exercised by that use case — **derived**, not asserted.
A story is linked to a use case when the use case exercises at least one requirement the story satisfies.

::: callout-important
## How to read the use case columns
There is no direct user story to use case link in the source material. The marks
below are inferred through the shared requirement: if a story satisfies `AD01`
and `UC02` exercises `AD01`, the story is shown against `UC02`. This is a
reasonable approximation for coverage checking, but it is not a stakeholder
assertion and should not be treated as traceability evidence until each story is
tagged to a use case directly.
:::

:::::::::: panel-tabset

## AD — Adaptability

7 stories in this category.

::: tbl-wrap
| User story | UC01 | UC02 | UC03 | UC04 | UC05 | UC06 | UC07 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [US-AD-01]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Ecologist]{.ug}<br>As an ecologist, I want to adapt an existing indicator workflow to a new ecosystem type without rewriting the full analysis, so that I can reuse established methods and save weeks of rework.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow's ecosystem-specific components are isolated in a documented config file/module; swapping to a new ecosystem requires editing only that file, not the core analysis code.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AD03]{.req} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
| [US-AD-02]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data analyst]{.ug}<br>As a data analyst, I want to understand which parts of a workflow are ecosystem-specific vs generic, so that I know exactly what to change when switching context.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow documentation includes an explicit table separating 'ecosystem-specific' from 'generic/reusable' components.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AD01]{.req} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-AD-03]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Government analyst]{.ug}<br>As a government analyst, I want to switch the assessment purpose (e.g. risk to recovery) without needing a new workflow from scratch, so that I can serve multiple reporting needs with one underlying system.<br>[**Acceptance:** A single workflow run accepts a 'purpose' parameter (e.g. risk / condition / recovery) that changes calculation and interpretation without altering the ecosystem or data inputs.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AD04]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
| [US-AD-04]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Ecologist]{.ug}<br>As an ecologist, I want to receive guidance on reconciling global and local data sources for the same ecosystem, so that my workflow is defensible, reproducible, and transparent.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow documentation includes a named reconciliation method for combining global and local/jurisdictional datasets, with the resampling or matching approach stated explicitly.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AD05]{.req} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |   |   |
| [US-AD-05]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Research Software Engineer]{.ug}<br>As an RSE, I want each workflow structured as numbered, self-contained notebooks (e.g. 01-data-download, 10-data-preparation, 20-calculate-indicator), so that individual steps can be re-run or replaced without re-running the entire pipeline.<br>[**Acceptance:** Each numbered notebook runs independently given the previous step's outputs; no step depends on in-memory state from another.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AD01]{.req} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-AD-06]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Research Software Engineer]{.ug}<br>As an RSE, I want a single workflow template (Quarto .qmd or R Markdown .Rmd) enforcing a consistent structure (metadata block, data sources, methods, outputs, known limitations), so that all workflows are comparable and cataloguable.<br>[**Acceptance:** A published template exists; every new workflow is generated from it and contains all five required sections.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AD03, RE01]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
| [US-AD-07]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Ecologist]{.ug}<br>As an ecologist, I want workflows to calculate indicator values aligned to specific IUCN RLE criteria (A: extent decline; B: restricted distribution; C: abiotic condition; D: biotic condition), so that outputs are directly usable in risk assessment documentation.<br>[**Acceptance:** Each workflow states which RLE criterion it addresses; output fields map to the values required by that criterion.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AD04, VO01]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
:::

## RE — Reproducibility and transparency

5 stories in this category.

::: tbl-wrap
| User story | UC01 | UC02 | UC03 | UC04 | UC05 | UC06 | UC07 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [US-RE-01]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data scientist]{.ug}<br>As a data scientist, I want to run a workflow developed by someone else on a new dataset without modifying the code, so that I can validate and replicate published assessments independently.<br>[**Acceptance:** A third party can clone the workflow repository, point it at a new dataset conforming to the documented input schema, and produce results without editing any source file.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** RE06]{.req} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
| [US-RE-02]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Research Software Engineer]{.ug}<br>As a research software engineer, I want to containerise the workflow environment with pinned dependencies, so that software versions don't break the workflow when R or packages change.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow ships with a container definition (Dockerfile or equivalent) pinning all package versions; a fresh container build reproduces identical output on a reference dataset.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** RE04]{.req} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |
| [US-RE-03]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Platform Administrator]{.ug}<br>As a platform administrator, I want each workflow to declare its software environment (R/Python version, package list with versions) in a machine-readable format (renv.lock or requirements.txt), so that the environment is reproducible anywhere.<br>[**Acceptance:** Environment file is present, version-pinned, and a clean rebuild from it runs the workflow to completion.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** RE04]{.req} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |
| [US-RE-04]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Environmental Policy Analyst / Reporting Officer]{.ug}<br>As a government reporting officer, I want each workflow run to produce a reproducibility record (timestamp, software environment snapshot, parameter values, input checksums), so that results can be independently verified.<br>[**Acceptance:** Every run emits a machine-readable record containing all four elements, stored alongside the outputs.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** RE01, RE02, RE03]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
| [US-RE-05]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Research Software Engineer]{.ug}<br>As an RSE, I want each workflow registered in the indicator catalogue with a DOI and codemeta.json, so that workflows are citable as research software outputs.<br>[**Acceptance:** Catalogue entry contains a resolvable DOI and a valid codemeta.json file.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** RE07]{.req} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |
:::

## VO — Classification and vocabularies

5 stories in this category.

::: tbl-wrap
| User story | UC01 | UC02 | UC03 | UC04 | UC05 | UC06 | UC07 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [US-VO-01]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Ecologist]{.ug}<br>As an ecologist, I want to map local ecosystem classifications to global typologies (e.g. IUCN GET), so that my assessments align with international standards.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow metadata includes a documented cross-reference between the local ecosystem classification used and the corresponding IUCN GET unit(s).]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** VO02]{.req} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
| [US-VO-02]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data manager]{.ug}<br>As a data manager, I want a curated vocabulary mapping between national and global ecosystem classifications, so that others don't have to reconcile it themselves each time.<br>[**Acceptance:** A published, versioned mapping table exists linking national classification codes to GET units, accessible independently of any single workflow.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** VO02, VO04]{.req} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
| [US-VO-03]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Indicator developer]{.ug}<br>As an indicator developer, I want vocabulary mapping to be machine-readable for workflow metadata, so that classification alignment can be automated rather than manual.<br>[**Acceptance:** The classification mapping is available in a machine-readable format (e.g. SKOS/CSV/JSON) that can be parsed programmatically, not only as prose documentation.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** VO04]{.req} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |
| [US-VO-04]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Policy officer]{.ug}<br>As a policy officer, I want ecosystem types linked to authoritative identifiers (IBRA, IUCN GET IDs), so that reporting references are unambiguous and citable.<br>[**Acceptance:** Each ecosystem type referenced in workflow outputs carries at least one authoritative identifier (e.g. IBRA region code, IUCN GET unit ID).]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** VO03]{.req} |   |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
| [US-VO-05]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Research Software Engineer]{.ug}<br>As an RSE, I want workflows to use GET vocabulary identifiers for ecosystem types in all metadata fields, so that outputs are semantically interoperable with other Australian and global ecosystem datasets.<br>[**Acceptance:** Every ecosystem reference in workflow metadata resolves to a GET unit identifier.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** VO01, VO03]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
:::

## DD — Data discovery

13 stories in this category.

::: tbl-wrap
| User story | UC01 | UC02 | UC03 | UC04 | UC05 | UC06 | UC07 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [US-DD-01]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data Scientist]{.ug}<br>As a data scientist, I want each catalogued dataset to expose machine-readable provenance, currency, and licence metadata, so that I can assess fitness-for-purpose before committing analysis time.<br>[**Acceptance:** Metadata record validates against a STAC Item schema; includes datetime, providers, license, and a provenance field conforming to W3C PROV-O.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD01, DD02]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |   |   |
| [US-DD-02]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data Scientist]{.ug}<br>As a data scientist, I want a documented transformation function that reconciles a national dataset with a global equivalent (CRS, resolution, temporal extent), so that I don't hand-roll reconciliation logic per workflow.<br>[**Acceptance:** Function accepts source + target CRS/grid, logs the resampling method used, and fails loudly (not silently) on unresolvable mismatches.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD03, AD05]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |
| [US-DD-03]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data Scientist]{.ug}<br>As a data scientist, I want known limitations and bias flags attached at the point of use, not buried in a separate PDF, so that downstream users can't miss them.<br>[**Acceptance:** Limitations field is a required, non-empty property in the workflow's metadata block.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD06]{.req} |   |   |   |   |   |   |   |
| [US-DD-04]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data Provider / Data Custodian]{.ug}<br>As a data custodian, I want to publish datasets with a persistent identifier and update-cadence declaration, so that consumers know whether "current" data is a live feed or a static snapshot.<br>[**Acceptance:** Dataset has a DOI or equivalent PID; update frequency stated in ISO 8601 duration format (e.g. P1Y for annual).]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD02, DD05]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |   |   |   |
| [US-DD-05]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Platform user]{.ug}<br>As a platform user, I want to know where ecosystem distribution data comes from and when it was last updated, so that I can assess its fitness for purpose before committing to an analysis.<br>[**Acceptance:** Each catalogued dataset entry states its source, last-updated date, and update frequency in a consistent, visible field.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD02]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |   |   |   |
| [US-DD-06]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Analyst — restricted data]{.ug}<br>As an analyst working with restricted data, I want to run the workflow within the platform where the data lives, so that I can comply with data governance requirements while still doing the analysis.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow can execute entirely within the hosting platform (e.g. CoESRA, NCI) without requiring the restricted dataset to be downloaded or copied elsewhere.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD05, AC04]{.req} |   |   |   |   |   |   |   |
| [US-DD-07]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Wetland ecologist]{.ug}<br>As a wetland ecologist, I want to integrate aerial survey data with satellite water extent time series, so that I can build a more complete picture of ecosystem condition.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow includes a documented step for combining aerial survey inputs with satellite time-series data, including how differing time steps/resolutions are aligned.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD04]{.req} |   |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |
| [US-DD-08]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data scientist]{.ug}<br>As a data scientist, I want guidance on transitioning from HPC preprocessing to cloud/local analysis, so that I'm not locked into one computing environment.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow documentation states which steps run locally, in the cloud, or on HPC, and what changes (if any) are needed to move between them.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD05]{.req} |   |   |   |   |   |   |   |
| [US-DD-09]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Marine ecologist]{.ug}<br>As a marine ecologist, I want to apply consistent indicator calculations across regions with uneven survey coverage, so that results remain comparable despite data gaps.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow calculation method is documented as producing comparable outputs regardless of uneven survey coverage across regions (e.g. via standardisation or a stated limitation where this isn't possible).]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD03]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |
| [US-DD-10]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Indicator developer]{.ug}<br>As an indicator developer, I want templates for harmonising heterogeneous survey datasets, so that I don't rebuild harmonisation logic for every new workflow.<br>[**Acceptance:** A reusable harmonisation template (script or function) exists that new workflows can call rather than re-implementing dataset harmonisation logic.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD03]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |
| [US-DD-11]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Data analyst]{.ug}<br>As a data analyst, I want clear documentation of data sources and known limitations embedded in each workflow, so that I can make informed fitness-for-purpose decisions before investing in an analysis.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow output or metadata includes a non-empty 'limitations and known biases' field before results are presented as final.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD06]{.req} |   |   |   |   |   |   |   |
| [US-DD-12]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Ecologist]{.ug}<br>As an ecologist, I want to access named datasets (DEA data cube, NARCliM2.0, TASVEG, CRU TS) via documented API calls or download scripts, so that data provenance is captured from the first pipeline step.<br>[**Acceptance:** Each named dataset has a documented access method (API endpoint or download script) that records source, retrieval date, and version in the workflow log.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD01, RE02]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |
| [US-DD-13]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Data Scientist]{.ug}<br>As a data scientist, I want an assessment check for each input dataset, so that I know which datasets are ready for use and which require transformation before entering a workflow.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow reports a per-dataset readiness status (ready / needs transformation) with the specific reason before calculation begins.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DD02]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |   |   |   |
:::

## DO — Documentation and training

8 stories in this category.

::: tbl-wrap
| User story | UC01 | UC02 | UC03 | UC04 | UC05 | UC06 | UC07 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [US-DO-01]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Non-coder ecologist]{.ug}<br>As a non-coder ecologist, I want step-by-step guidance with plain-language explanations at every stage, so that I can run the workflow without needing programming expertise.<br>[**Acceptance:** Documentation includes a plain-language, numbered walkthrough usable by someone with no coding background, validated by at least one non-coder test read.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DO01]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-DO-02]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Mid-career data scientist]{.ug}<br>As a mid-career data scientist, I want documentation explaining what each workflow function does and why it exists, so that I can modify components confidently for new use cases.<br>[**Acceptance:** Each workflow function has an accompanying description of its purpose and behaviour, accessible without reading the source code.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DO04]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-DO-03]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Senior scientist]{.ug}<br>As a senior scientist, I want documentation of how uncertainty is quantified and communicated in the outputs, so that I can defend the workflow's results to government decision-makers.<br>[**Acceptance:** Documentation explicitly states the uncertainty quantification method used and how confidence should be communicated to a non-technical decision-maker.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DO05, VA03]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-DO-04]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Workshop participant]{.ug}<br>As a workshop participant, I want worked examples covering common Australian ecosystem types, so that I can use the workflow as a template rather than starting from scratch.<br>[**Acceptance:** At least one worked example exists for a common Australian ecosystem type, runnable end-to-end as a template.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DO02]{.req} |   |   |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-DO-05]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Team leader]{.ug}<br>As a team leader, I want training materials that accommodate different learning levels within the same team, so that everyone can contribute regardless of technical background.<br>[**Acceptance:** Training materials are tiered (e.g. beginner/intermediate/advanced) so a mixed-skill team can each start at an appropriate level.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DO06]{.req} |   |   |   |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-DO-06]{.sid} [Need]{.layer-need}<br>[Platform administrator]{.ug}<br>As a platform administrator, I want workshops supported by published, reusable data and code outputs, so that participants have concrete materials to reference after the session ends.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workshop or training session outputs (code, data, slides) are published to a persistent, shareable location before the session ends.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DO03]{.req} |   |   |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-DO-07]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Research Software Engineer]{.ug}<br>As an RSE, I want each workflow to include a data flow diagram (.dot or Mermaid) showing inputs, transformation steps, and outputs, so that I can understand the pipeline structure before running or modifying it.<br>[**Acceptance:** Diagram source file is version-controlled alongside the workflow and renders in the workflow documentation.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DO04]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-DO-08]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Environmental Policy Analyst / Reporting Officer]{.ug}<br>As a government reporting officer, I want indicator outputs delivered as standardised tabular summaries (CSV with a defined column schema) and spatial layers (cloud-optimised GeoTIFF), so that I can ingest them into reporting pipelines without reformatting.<br>[**Acceptance:** Published column schema exists and outputs validate against it; raster outputs are valid COGs.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** DO07, AC05]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |
:::

## AC — Accessibility

3 stories in this category.

::: tbl-wrap
| User story | UC01 | UC02 | UC03 | UC04 | UC05 | UC06 | UC07 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [US-AC-01]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Ecologist]{.ug}<br>As an ecologist, I want to run a workflow on EcoCommons (cloud notebook) and locally (R/RStudio or Python) without modifying any code, so that I am not dependent on a single platform.<br>[**Acceptance:** Same workflow produces identical outputs on both platforms from the same inputs; no platform-specific paths hard-coded.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AC01, RE06]{.req} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |
| [US-AC-02]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Platform Administrator]{.ug}<br>As a platform administrator, I want compute and memory requirements specified per workflow, so that I can provision appropriate resources on Nectar or NCI without trial and error.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow metadata states minimum and recommended CPU, RAM, and storage, validated against at least one benchmark run.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AC07]{.req} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |
| [US-AC-03]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Environmental Policy Analyst / Reporting Officer]{.ug}<br>As a government reporting officer, I want to access the catalogue and filter by ecosystem type (GET level), IUCN RLE criterion, or state/territory, so that I can identify available workflows for my reporting jurisdiction.<br>[**Acceptance:** Catalogue supports all three filters and returns workflows matching any combination of them.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** AC06]{.req} |   | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |
:::

## VA — Validation

2 stories in this category.

::: tbl-wrap
| User story | UC01 | UC02 | UC03 | UC04 | UC05 | UC06 | UC07 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [US-VA-01]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Ecologist]{.ug}<br>As an ecologist, I want workflows to validate input data against minimum quality thresholds (spatial coverage, completeness, temporal resolution) before running calculations, so that invalid inputs are caught early with informative error messages.<br>[**Acceptance:** Workflow halts with a named threshold and the observed value when an input fails; passing inputs are logged with their measured values.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** VA01]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   |   |
| [US-VA-02]{.sid} [Spec]{.layer-spec}<br>[Ecologist]{.ug}<br>As an ecologist, I want indicator values to include uncertainty estimates where methodologically appropriate, so that outputs communicate confidence for decision-making contexts.<br>[**Acceptance:** Outputs carry an uncertainty field, or an explicit statement of why uncertainty could not be quantified for that indicator.]{.ac}<br>[**Satisfies:** VA03, VA05]{.req} | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |   | [✓]{.mk-d} |   |   |
:::

::::::::::

## Coverage summary

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Total user stories | 43 |
| Need layer (from workshops) | 27 |
| Spec layer (implementation) | 16 |
| Stories with no derived use case | 4 |

### Stories per requirement category

| Category | Stories |
|---|---|
| AD — Adaptability | 7 |
| RE — Reproducibility and transparency | 5 |
| VO — Classification and vocabularies | 5 |
| DD — Data discovery | 13 |
| DO — Documentation and training | 8 |
| AC — Accessibility | 3 |
| VA — Validation | 2 |

The distribution is uneven by design of the source material rather than by
intent. Data discovery carries 13 stories while validation carries
2; validation was the least-developed theme in both workshops, and the
same imbalance appears in the requirement to use case matrix, where `VA04` and
`VA06` have no use case at all.

### Stories with no derived use case

`US-DD-03`, `US-DD-06`, `US-DD-08`, `US-DD-11`

These satisfy requirements that no current use case exercises, so they are the clearest evidence for which new use cases are needed.

::: callout-warning
## Status
Acceptance criteria were drafted from the story text rather than supplied by
stakeholders, and all stories remain pending review. Use case marks are derived,
not asserted.
:::
